units.translation: Thus Dobree for πλὴν ἐμοῦ [except me].
[It is uncertain whether καθ᾿ ἕν [one by one] at line 316 is said for καθάπαξ [once for all], about which I have spoken under the word ἀνέκαθεν [from the beginning].]
εἶ for εἷς [one] Canter, Eum. 200.
Eteocles, one man among many throughout the city, would be hymned.
And she carries beneath her one man of the Cadmeans.
But this deed was done by all in return for one.
One man having caused the greatest toil to his enemies.
From one rush.
To lead one man of all sheep-nurturing Asia.
All with one stroke.
One woman having destroyed many lives.
One woman having destroyed the lives of many men.
From one road.
A single vote, publicly exacted from the city, has been decided.
These fell from one ship.
Having obtained one hope after many had been shattered.
From one womb.
In one blow.
In one day.
With one mind.
For the city to suffer one public wound.
This is already one of the three wrestling bouts.
The clash is not of one spear.
There is no one except one who could shear him.
For someone pouring out everything in return for one blood.
For many desires fall together into one.
Saying that some should do one thing, and others should do nothing.
